```{r}
# Multicollinearity testing (wet/dry season) across elephant
# populations: KAZA, Etosha, and Western (Kunene + Omusati)

# ---- 0. Packages ----
library(terra)
library(usdm)
library(corrplot)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

setwd("~/Desktop/Arnhold/sparcle-hwc/code")

# 1. Paths and constants

base_dir <- "~/Desktop/Arnhold/sparcle-hwc-old2/code/sparcle-hwc/data"

# Static covariates + EVI (shared across ALL populations)
static_folder <- file.path(base_dir, "500m_data")
evi_folder    <- file.path(static_folder, "EVI data")

# Annual "distance to land cover type" rasters (2008-2020, one per type/year)
lc_dist_folder <- file.path(base_dir, "ESACCI_LCCS", "lc_dist_2")
lc_types       <- c("cropland", "grassland", "shrubland", "tree_cover", "urban", "water")
lc_dist_years  <- 2008:2020

# Movement data (one source per population)
kaza_file      <- file.path(base_dir, "elephant_2010-Feb2020.csv")                 # single CSV, multiple individuals
etosha_folder  <- file.path(base_dir, "Elephant movements", "Etosha")              # one CSV per individual
kunene_folder  <- file.path(base_dir, "Elephant movements", "Kunene")              # one CSV per individual
omusati_folder <- file.path(base_dir, "Elephant movements", "Omusati")             # one CSV per individual

coord_x    <- "Lon"
coord_y    <- "Lat"
target_crs <- "EPSG:4326"

# Kept for reference only -- not applied, since all rasters are already the
# same CRS/resolution/extent (or are padded to match via extend(), see below).
my_extent <- ext(12.5, 25.5, -21.5, -16.5)

wet_months <- c(11, 12, 1, 2, 3, 4)   # Nov - Apr
dry_months <- c(5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10)    # May - Oct



# 2. Helper functions

#2a. Raster prep 

# Print CRS/resolution/extent/layer-count for a set of raster files.
# Useful for diagnosing a "geometry mismatch" warning/error.
diagnose_rasters <- function(files) {
  for (f in files) {
    r <- rast(f)
    cat("\n---", basename(f), "---\n")
    cat("CRS:   ", crs(r, describe = TRUE)$name, "\n")
    cat("Res:   ", paste(res(r), collapse = " x "), "\n")
    cat("Extent:", paste(round(as.vector(ext(r)), 5), collapse = ", "), "\n")
    cat("Dim:   ", paste(dim(r)[1:2], collapse = " x "), "\n")
    cat("Layers:", nlyr(r), "\n")
  }
}

# Load a set of static covariate rasters. If a raster's CRS/resolution match the template but its extent is smaller (e.g. missing rows), pad it with extend(), preserves the original pixel values exactly (no
# interpolation)
load_static_covariates <- function(files, template = NULL) {
  r_list <- lapply(files, rast)
  names(r_list) <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(files))

  if (is.null(template)) template <- r_list[[1]]

  r_list <- lapply(r_list, function(r) {
    if (!compareGeom(r, template, stopOnError = FALSE)) r <- extend(r, template)
    r
  })

  for (nm in names(r_list)) {
    if (!compareGeom(r_list[[nm]], template, stopOnError = FALSE)) {
      warning("Still a mismatch after extend() for raster: ", nm,
              " -- this likely needs project()/resample(), not just padding.")
    }
  }

  out <- rast(r_list)

  # nm for single-band files, nm_1/nm_2/... for multi-band files
  layer_names <- unlist(mapply(function(r, nm) {
    if (nlyr(r) == 1) nm else paste0(nm, "_", 1:nlyr(r))
  }, r_list, names(r_list), SIMPLIFY = FALSE))
  names(out) <- layer_names

  out
}

# Load a single EVI raster for one year/season, matching it to the template geometry. Tries extend() first (cheap, exact); falls back to resample() only if extend() alone isn't enough.
prep_evi_raster <- function(file, template, layer_name) {
  r <- rast(file)

  if (!compareGeom(r, template, stopOnError = FALSE)) r <- extend(r, template)

  if (!compareGeom(r, template, stopOnError = FALSE)) {
    warning("Raster '", layer_name, "' (", basename(file), ") still doesn't match ",
            "the template after extend() -- falling back to resample().")
    r <- resample(r, template, method = "bilinear")
  }

  names(r) <- layer_name
  r
}

# Load a multi-band ANNUAL time-series raster 
load_annual_raster <- function(file, template) {
  r <- rast(file)
  if (!compareGeom(r, template, stopOnError = FALSE)) r <- extend(r, template)
  if (!compareGeom(r, template, stopOnError = FALSE)) {
    warning("Raster '", basename(file), "' still doesn't match the template ",
            "after extend() -- falling back to resample().")
    r <- resample(r, template, method = "bilinear")
  }
  r
}

# Build a multi-band ANNUAL time-series stack from a set of single-band, single-year files
# Each file is aligned to `template` (via extend(), falling back to resample() if needed) and stacked with band names set to the year, so the result can be used with match_year_band() exactly like worldpop_stack.
build_annual_stack_from_files <- function(folder, file_prefix, years, template) {
  r_list <- lapply(years, function(yr) {
    f <- file.path(folder, paste0(file_prefix, yr, ".tif"))
    if (!file.exists(f)) {
      warning("Missing file for '", file_prefix, "' year ", yr, ": ", f)
      return(NULL)
    }
    r <- rast(f)
    if (!compareGeom(r, template, stopOnError = FALSE)) r <- extend(r, template)
    if (!compareGeom(r, template, stopOnError = FALSE)) {
      warning("Raster '", basename(f), "' still doesn't match the template ",
              "after extend() -- falling back to resample().")
      r <- resample(r, template, method = "bilinear")
    }
    names(r) <- as.character(yr)
    r
  })

  r_list <- Filter(Negate(is.null), r_list)
  if (length(r_list) == 0) stop("No files found for prefix: ", file_prefix)

  do.call(c, r_list)
}

# Pick band matching `target_year` from an annual time-series stack (band names must be the years, e.g. "2000", "2001", ...). 
match_year_band <- function(stack, target_year, layer_name) {
  available_years <- as.numeric(names(stack))

  yr_to_use <- if (as.character(target_year) %in% names(stack)) {
    target_year
  } else {
    nearest <- available_years[which.min(abs(available_years - target_year))]
    warning("No exact '", layer_name, "' band for year ", target_year,
            " -- using nearest available year (", nearest, ") instead.")
    nearest
  }

  r <- stack[[as.character(yr_to_use)]]
  names(r) <- layer_name
  r
}

#2b. Movement data loading

# Some sources (e.g. Movebank exports for Etosha/Kunene/Omusati) use different column names than the KAZA data. read.csv() auto-converts
# hyphens to dots, so "location-long" becomes "location.long", etc. This maps those onto the common Lon/Lat/ID schema the rest of the script expects, without touching data that's already in that schema.
standardize_movement_columns <- function(df) {
  if (!coord_x %in% names(df) && "location.long" %in% names(df)) {
    df[[coord_x]] <- df[["location.long"]]
  }
  if (!coord_y %in% names(df) && "location.lat" %in% names(df)) {
    df[[coord_y]] <- df[["location.lat"]]
  }
  if (!"ID" %in% names(df) && "tag.local.identifier" %in% names(df)) {
    df$ID <- df[["tag.local.identifier"]]
  }
  df
}

# KAZA-style source: a single CSV containing multiple individuals.
load_movement_csv <- function(file) {
  df <- read.csv(file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  standardize_movement_columns(df)
}

# Etosha/Western-style source: a folder containing one CSV per individual.
# Adds an ID column (preferring tag-local-identifier, falling back to the filename) if one isn't already present.
load_movement_folder <- function(folder, pattern = "\\.csv$") {
  files <- list.files(folder, pattern = pattern, full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE)
  if (length(files) == 0) stop("No CSV files found in: ", folder)
  message("  Found ", length(files), " individual CSV(s) in: ", folder)

  df_list <- lapply(files, function(f) {
    df <- read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    df <- standardize_movement_columns(df)
    if (!"ID" %in% names(df)) df$ID <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(f))
    df
  })

  bind_rows(df_list)
}

# Ensure a movement data frame has numeric `year` and `month` columns, deriving them from a date/timestamp column if not already present.
ensure_year_month <- function(df, date_col = NULL) {
  if (all(c("year", "month") %in% names(df))) return(df)

  if (is.null(date_col)) {
    date_col <- if ("date" %in% names(df)) "date"
    else if ("DT" %in% names(df)) "DT"
    else if ("timestamp" %in% names(df)) "timestamp"
    else stop("No 'year'/'month' columns and no 'date'/'DT'/'timestamp' column to derive them from.")
  }

  parsed <- lubridate::parse_date_time(
    df[[date_col]],
    orders = c("mdy HM", "mdy HMS", "mdy", "ymd HMS", "ymd HM", "ymd", "dmy HM", "dmy")
  )

  df$year  <- lubridate::year(parsed)
  df$month <- lubridate::month(parsed)
  df
}

#2c. Season assignment 

# Add `season` (wet/dry) and `wet_year` (the calendar year the wet season
# STARTED in, since wet season runs Nov -> Apr and crosses the year boundary)
add_season_columns <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(
      season   = ifelse(month %in% wet_months, "wet", "dry"),
      wet_year = ifelse(month %in% c(11, 12), year, year - 1)
    )
}

#2d. Core collinearity extraction 

make_pts <- function(df) {
  pts <- vect(df, geom = c(coord_x, coord_y), crs = "EPSG:4326")
  project(pts, target_crs)
}

# For one population + one season: loop through each year present, pull the matching seasonal EVI raster, the matching annual worldPop band, AND the matching annual band for each "distance to land cover type" raster
# extract static + EVI + worldPop + land-cover-distance covariate values at that year's points, combine across years, then run a correlation plot + VIF.
#   elephant_df: movement data already filtered to one season
#   season_label: label for messages/plot titles, e.g. "KAZA - Dry Season"
#   evi_season: "dry" or "wet" -- controls the EVI filename pattern
#   year_col: "year" for dry season, "wet_year" for wet season
run_multicollinearity_by_year <- function(elephant_df, season_label, evi_season, year_col) {

  message("Processing: ", season_label)

  years <- sort(unique(elephant_df[[year_col]]))
  message("  Years present: ", paste(years, collapse = ", "))

  all_vals <- list()

  for (yr in years) {

    df_yr <- elephant_df[elephant_df[[year_col]] == yr, ]
    if (nrow(df_yr) == 0) next

    pts_yr <- make_pts(df_yr)

    evi_file <- if (evi_season == "dry") {
      file.path(evi_folder, paste0("evi_dry_", yr, ".tif"))
    } else {
      file.path(evi_folder, paste0("evi_wet_", yr, "_", yr + 1, ".tif"))
    }

    if (!file.exists(evi_file)) {
      warning("  Missing EVI file for ", season_label, " ", yr, ": ", evi_file,
              " -- skipping this year")
      next
    }

    evi_r      <- prep_evi_raster(evi_file, static_template, "evi")
    worldpop_r <- match_year_band(worldpop_stack, yr, "worldpop")

    # One band per land cover type, matched to this year (nearest-year
    # fallback happens inside match_year_band, e.g. for years outside
    # 2008-2020, same handling as worldpop).
    lc_dist_r <- lapply(names(lc_dist_stacks), function(lt) {
      match_year_band(lc_dist_stacks[[lt]], yr, paste0("dist_", lt))
    })

    covariates_yr <- c(static_stack, evi_r, worldpop_r, do.call(c, lc_dist_r))

    vals_yr <- terra::extract(covariates_yr, pts_yr)
    vals_yr <- vals_yr[, -1]  # drop the auto ID column added by terra::extract

    all_vals[[as.character(yr)]] <- vals_yr
  }

  elephant_vals <- bind_rows(all_vals)
  elephant_vals <- na.omit(elephant_vals)
  elephant_vals_curated <- elephant_vals %>%
  select(-gpw_rast_500m_1, -gpw_rast_500m_2, -gpw_rast_500m_3, -gpw_rast_500m_4, -gpw_rast_500m_5, -distance_to_landcover_img_500m_1, -distance_to_landcover_img_500m_2, -distance_to_landcover_img_500m_3, -distance_to_landcover_img_500m_4, -core_dist_rast_500m)

  corrplot(cor(elephant_vals_curated), method = "number", type = "upper", tl.cex = 0.7, number.cex = 0.5,
           title = paste("Correlation -", season_label), mar = c(0, 0, 1, 0))

  vif_result <- vifstep(elephant_vals_curated, th = 10)
  print(vif_result)
  final_vars <- vif_result@results$Variables

  list(elephant_vals = elephant_vals, vif_result = vif_result, final_vars = final_vars)
}

# For one population: add season columns, split wet/dry, and run the collinearity test for both seasons.
run_population <- function(population_name, movement_df) {
  message("\n===== ", population_name, " =====")

  movement_df <- add_season_columns(movement_df)
  dry_df <- movement_df %>% filter(season == "dry")
  wet_df <- movement_df %>% filter(season == "wet")

  dry_results <- run_multicollinearity_by_year(
    elephant_df  = dry_df,
    season_label = paste(population_name, "- Dry Season"),
    evi_season   = "dry",
    year_col     = "year"
  )

  wet_results <- run_multicollinearity_by_year(
    elephant_df  = wet_df,
    season_label = paste(population_name, "- Wet Season"),
    evi_season   = "wet",
    year_col     = "wet_year"
  )

  list(dry = dry_results, wet = wet_results)
}




# 3.  Load static covariates (shared across all populations)

# world pop loaded separately below and matched to each point's own year, same as EVI.
static_files <- list.files(static_folder, pattern = "\\.tif$", full.names = TRUE)
static_files <- static_files[!grepl("worldPop_comb_img_500m\\.tif$", static_files)]
print(static_files)

static_stack    <- load_static_covariates(static_files)
static_template <- static_stack[[1]]
print(static_stack)

# worldPop: annual time series, matched per point-year 
worldpop_file  <- file.path(static_folder, "worldPop_comb_img_500m.tif")
worldpop_stack <- load_annual_raster(worldpop_file, static_template)
names(worldpop_stack)  # should show "2000".."2020" -- confirms band-year mapping

#Distance to land cover type rasters: annyal time series (2008-2020)
#matches per point-year, same as worldpop and EVI 
#cropland, grassland, shrubland, tree cover, urvan, and water covariates 
#File names "dist_type_year.tif", one band per file, stacked
lc_dist_stacks <- setNames(
  lapply(lc_types, function(lt) {
    build_annual_stack_from_files(
      folder      = lc_dist_folder,
      file_prefix = paste0("dist_", lt, "_"),
      years       = lc_dist_years,
      template    = static_template
    )
  }),
  lc_types
)

# check: each stack should show bands "2008".."2020"
lapply(lc_dist_stacks, names)




# 4. LOAD MOVEMENT DATA PER POPULATION

# KAZA: single CSV, multiple individuals, already has year/month 
kaza_data <- load_movement_csv(kaza_file) %>% ensure_year_month()

# Etosha: one CSV per individual
etosha_data <- load_movement_folder(etosha_folder) %>% ensure_year_month()

# Western: Kunene + Omusati combined, one CSV per individual in each 
western_data <- bind_rows(
  load_movement_folder(kunene_folder),
  load_movement_folder(omusati_folder)
) %>% ensure_year_month()



# 5. Run multicollinearity test for all populations


all_results <- list(
  KAZA    = run_population("KAZA",    kaza_data),
  Etosha  = run_population("Etosha",  etosha_data),
  Western = run_population("Western", western_data)
)


#6. Summary

for (pop in names(all_results)) {
  cat("\n===", pop, "===\n")
  cat("Dry season retained variables:\n"); print(all_results[[pop]]$dry$final_vars)
  cat("Wet season retained variables:\n"); print(all_results[[pop]]$wet$final_vars)
}

# Individual results 
# all_results$KAZA$dry$vif_result
# all_results$Etosha$wet$elephant_vals
# all_results$Western$dry$final_vars
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# 7. EXPORT RESULTS
# ============================================================
 
export_dir <- file.path(base_dir, "outputs", "multicollinearity_results")
dir.create(export_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
 
# For one population/season result: write the VIF table, correlation matrix,
# retained-variable list, extracted covariate values, and a corrplot image.
export_results <- function(results, population_name, season_label, export_dir) {
  prefix <- file.path(export_dir, paste0(population_name, "_", season_label))
 
  write.csv(results$vif_result@results, paste0(prefix, "_VIF.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(cor(results$elephant_vals), paste0(prefix, "_correlation_matrix.csv"))
  writeLines(results$final_vars, paste0(prefix, "_final_variables.txt"))
  write.csv(results$elephant_vals, paste0(prefix, "_covariate_values.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
 
  png(paste0(prefix, "_corrplot.png"), width = 1600, height = 1600, res = 200)
  corrplot(cor(results$elephant_vals), method = "number", type = "upper", tl.cex = 0.7,
           title = paste("Correlation -", population_name, season_label), mar = c(0, 0, 1, 0))
  dev.off()
 
  message("Exported: ", basename(prefix), "_*")
}
 
for (pop in names(all_results)) {
  export_results(all_results[[pop]]$dry, pop, "Dry", export_dir)
  export_results(all_results[[pop]]$wet, pop, "Wet", export_dir)
}
 
# One combined CSV across every population/season, for quick side-by-side comparison
summary_table <- bind_rows(lapply(names(all_results), function(pop) {
  bind_rows(
    all_results[[pop]]$dry$vif_result@results %>% mutate(Population = pop, Season = "Dry"),
    all_results[[pop]]$wet$vif_result@results %>% mutate(Population = pop, Season = "Wet")
  )
})) %>%
  select(Population, Season, Variables, VIF)
 
write.csv(summary_table, file.path(export_dir, "all_populations_VIF_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
 
message("\nAll results exported to: ", export_dir)
```
